newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan to boost oil output, start exporting.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan to boost oil output, start exporting.

text.p: Uzbekistan plans to raise output of oil and gas condensate to 10 million tonnes (200,000 barrels per day) by 2000 from eight million tonnes (160,000 bpd) this year and to become an oil exporter, an official said on Tuesday.

"Taking into account that today we meet our own needs of eight million tonnes of crude oil a year, it is beyond all doubt that Uzbekistan will become an oil exporter in the next century," Ibrat Zainutdinov, deputy chairman of the national corporation Uzbekneftegaz, told a news conference.

He said the increase in output would come from development of new fields by foreign firms and that Uzbekneftegaz was in negotiations with Italy's Agip SpA, U.S.-based Mobil Corp and the Japan National Oil Corporation on various production projects.
He said France's Technip would complete construction of the first part of an oil refinery near the town of Bukhara in the south of the Central Asian state in June.
The facility will process 2.5 million tonnes of gas condensate a year.
Japan's Mitsui & Co Ltd has started the reconstruction of an oil refinery in the town of Fergana in the east of the country, he said.
According to Uzbekneftegas estimates, Uzbekistan's hydrocarbon reserves comprise 4.4 billion tonnes of oil, 629 million tonnes of gas condensate and 5.429 trillion cubic metres of natural gas.
